source.identity: Billy & Jimmy — Double Dragon II: The Revenge — NES

source is a static PNG and does not establish source-authentic exposure durations
INFERRED: all dual-anchor force-couple mechanics, torque sign, root/COM response, release order, spacing, cadence, overshoot, and recovery

relationship.force_rule: two closed separated anchors may carry equal-opposed forces whose net translation is small but moment is nonzero
relationship.topology_rule: contact topology changes only after the released anchor is visibly unloaded to zero
relationship.release_rule: upper unload -> upper release -> lower unload -> lower release

keys.name: SEPARATE_READ
keys.causal_role: establish independent support and negative space before eligibility
keys.root_com_note: both roots independently stacked; no shared force or custody

keys.name: ELIGIBLE_APPROACH
keys.causal_role: close distance while both bodies remain independently supported and contact-eligible
keys.root_com_note: COMs commit inward before any anchor is allowed to close

keys.name: UPPER_TOUCH_ZERO
keys.causal_role: earn first contact anchor without granting force authority
keys.root_com_note: upper hands overlap at zero load; both ground supports still own their roots

keys.name: DUAL_TOUCH_ZERO
keys.causal_role: close second anchor while both contacts remain unloaded
keys.root_com_note: two separated anchors define a moment arm but still carry no force

keys.name: COUPLE_PRELOAD
keys.causal_role: raise equal-opposed anchor loads after dual-contact topology is already established
keys.root_com_note: opposed separated forces create torque while net horizontal translation stays small

keys.name: COUPLE_MAX_ROTATION
keys.causal_role: show maximum torque as counter-rotation and support-edge commitment rather than translation
keys.root_com_note: roots stay nearly fixed; torsos rotate opposite around braced support edges and COMs bank

keys.name: UPPER_UNLOAD_ZERO
keys.causal_role: remove upper force while upper contact remains closed, converting pure couple into lower-anchor resultant
keys.root_com_note: both anchors still closed; loss of upper force exposes a real lower-anchor resultant and starts shear

keys.name: UPPER_RELEASE
keys.causal_role: open the already-unloaded upper topology while lower anchor still carries force
keys.root_com_note: upper topology opens only after zero load; lower resultant shears A left and B right while the surviving anchor remains fixed

keys.name: LOWER_UNLOAD_ZERO
keys.causal_role: pay lower-anchor force debt while preserving last contact for one beat
keys.root_com_note: last anchor still touches at zero load as roots continue separating on unequal inertial clocks

keys.name: LOWER_RELEASE
keys.causal_role: open final contact only after its load has reached zero
keys.root_com_note: final topology opens after zero load; arms recoil locally and bodies retain distinct angular/translational debt

keys.name: SPLIT_OVERSHOOT
keys.causal_role: let the two bodies overshoot on unequal post-release clocks
keys.root_com_note: A overshoots farther left while B lags right; braking supports and torso leans oppose unequal debts

keys.name: DISPLACED_SETTLE
keys.causal_role: settle into a displaced asymmetric recovery rather than returning to the opening arrangement
keys.root_com_note: both bodies restack at new displaced positions with residual facing asymmetry and preserved negative space

compile.engine: Motion Dungeon ASCII-only deterministic key renderer

rounds.highest_value_visible_defect: post-release roots collapsed inward and open arms still pointed at retired relationship anchors, destroying split silhouette and making release read like continued grapple
rounds.same_body_correction: retract open limbs to body-local space; reverse post-unload root travel so lower-anchor resultant opens negative space; make A overshoot farther than B and settle displaced

rounds.evidence: actual 30-frame H.264 render visually inspected as filmstrip; dual-contact couple, zero-load-before-release, topology openings, unequal overshoot and displaced settle read distinctly
